Comparison and Contrast Paragraph
Comparison shows similarities between persons, places, things, ideas, or situations. On the other hand, contrast points out the differences between persons, places, things, ideas, or situations.

When writing a comparison and contrast paragraph, your topic sentence should identify both subjects to be compared or contrasted. It should also tell the reader exactly what you are going to say about these items. Then, include three key points of difference or similarity  in the body of your paragraph.Each point should provide examples that demonstrate similarities or differences. The concluding sentence reinforces the controlling idea (main idea).
Here are linking words that express comparison or contrast in these types of paragraphs.  </br></br>See the chart below.

Writing Tip: Linking Words that Express Concession/Contrast

You can use a variety of words and phrases to link your ideas and add coherence within a paragraph. When you want to write about a concession(a contrast between a predicted action and a circumstance) you can use conjunctions, adverbs or prepositions to link your ideas.

Conjunctions: A conjunction is a connecting word. although = though /even though = even if
For example:
I was happy to watch the movies even though I had seen it with some friends the previous week.

You can use these at the beginning of the clauses they introduce.
For example:
Although Amy and Peter are a couple, there will be some challenges for them in the future.
When you use however at the beginning of a sentence, you need to use a comma after it.

You can place though at the end of the sentence.
For example:
They are not together now. They love each other though.

Adverbs: Adverbs are verbs that describe or modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.

For example:
Verb:The building was built gradually.(In this case, the adverb "gradually' describes the verb "built".)
Adjective:The building has very large stones. (In this case, the adverb "very" modifies the adjective "large".)
Adverb:The architect is almost always right.(In this case, the adverb "almost" modifies the adverb "always".)

For example:
They haven't met him yet.
He was determined, nevertheless, to ensure the night was a great success.
She was to attend; however, her flight was late.

Prepositions: A preposition is a word or group of words that indicates location or relationship between a noun or pronoun and other parts of the sentence. These are followed by a noun or a gerund. across = beside = between = through

For example:
Once I knew I was on the right career path, I was prepared to move across the country.
I would never want to get in between the two of you.
Everyone needs to jump through hoops during their career.

images.text: Amy and Peter are different in almost every aspect of their life. Firstly, their approaches to relationships are quite distinct. Rational and level-headed, Amy deals with situations in a logical manner. She is not caught up in needless emotional mind games or requires validation from her partner. She doesn't dwell on past mistakes and is prepared to speak her mind when she feels she is not being heard. In comparison, Peter's sensitive nature can leave him feeling apprehensive to change and insecure in his relationships. This internal anxiety can manifest itself as inappropriate behavior and a lack of self-esteem. He can appear thoughtless and controlling. Often, he can dwell on situations that are completely inconsequential.

Another way this couple differ is their mindset towards life. Amy is optimistic about the future. She is ready to embrace life and tackle any challenges with positive energy and enthusiasm. Conversely, Peter's pessimistic outlook overrides most situations. He tends to prescribe to the glass half empty philosophy, as a way to protect himself and to handle any possible negative outcome.  Finally, how they approach their jobs reflects their personalities. Amy's job as a life coach encourages others to reach their personal goals. She focuses on establishing balanced lifestyles and inner confidence. Her gregarious, uplifting spirit coupled with her dislike for excuses and negative self talk, is a breath of fresh air to her overwhelmed clients.

Furthermore, Amy has her own goals and is highly motivated to succeed. On the other hand, Peter is happily unemployed. He rarely felt the need to overextend himself in a work environment. In fact, the times he was prepared to work longer hours were based on an assumption that he would be rewarded monetarily or through promotions. Furthermore, he enjoyed negotiating his own position; however, he was often silenced by management. He was unable to handle constructive criticism, yet was quick to point out the flaws of others.  Overall, these two lovebirds are polar opposites and will need to make some serious decisions in the future.
